note: Questions from the CBSE Class X Science board exam 2026, Q.P. code 31/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. This paper is split into Biology, Chemistry and Physics sections; the portal places its questions into board-pattern sections by type and marks. Questions that need a figure or a drawing are left out (Q2, Q12, Q33, Q37), and so is Q6, whose wording is ambiguous. Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which structure in a leaf is mainly responsible for gaseous exchange ?
questions.solution: Stomata are the tiny pores in the leaf through which gases (CO₂ and O₂) are exchanged.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Identify the correct statement for spirogyra, leishmania and hydra :
questions.solution: Spirogyra reproduces by fragmentation, Leishmania by binary fission and Hydra by budding, all asexual methods. (Leishmania is unicellular while the other two are multicellular, so B and C are wrong.)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Human brain has various parts or regions that help in different actions, responses and coordination. From the following, identify the part responsible for precision of voluntary actions :
questions.solution: The cerebellum maintains posture and balance and makes voluntary actions precise (for example picking up a pencil).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Pancreas secretes pancreatic juice which contain certain enzyme that helps in digestion of food. Choose the correct option from the following :
options: Trypsin digests emulsified fats and lipase digests proteins.
Trypsin digests proteins and lipase digests emulsified fats.
Trypsin and lipase both digests fats.
Trypsin digests proteins and lipase digests carbohydrates.
questions.solution: Trypsin digests proteins and lipase breaks down emulsified fats.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which of the following group is not 'biodegradable' ?
options: Polythene bag, rubber band, ball pen
questions.solution: Polythene, synthetic rubber bands and plastic ball pens cannot be broken down by microorganisms, so they are non-biodegradable.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Reflex actions do not involve thinking.
Reason (R): Most reflex actions are controlled by the spinal cord.
options: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Reflexes are automatic and do not involve thinking, because the reflex arc is completed in the spinal cord without the thinking part of the brain. So both are true and R explains A.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): In human beings, the respiratory pigment is haemoglobin present in red blood cells.
Reason (R): Haemoglobin has a very high affinity for carbon dioxide.
options: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Haemoglobin in red blood cells is the respiratory pigment, so A is true. It has a very high affinity for oxygen; carbon dioxide is mostly carried dissolved in plasma. So R is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) AgNO₃ + NaCl → NaNO₃ + AgCl
(ii) K₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2KCl
Which of the following options clearly describes both the reactions ?
options: (i) is double displacement, (ii) is displacement reaction.
Both, (i) and (ii) are displacement reactions and precipitation reactions.
Both, (i) and (ii) are double displacement reactions and precipitation reactions.
(i) is displacement, (ii) is double displacement reaction.
questions.solution: In both, the ions are exchanged (double displacement) and an insoluble solid forms (AgCl and BaSO₄), so both are double displacement and precipitation reactions.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which one of the following can be used as an acid-base indicator by a visually impaired (blind) student ?
questions.solution: Vanilla essence is an olfactory indicator: its smell disappears in a basic solution, so it can be used without seeing a colour change.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The gases evolved on heating lead (II) nitrate crystals are :
questions.solution: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂. Brown nitrogen dioxide and oxygen are given off.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The formula of functional group for aldehyde is :
questions.solution: Aldehydes have the –CHO group. –COOH is a carboxylic acid, >C=O within the chain is a ketone and –OH is an alcohol.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which of the following is a poor conductor of electricity ?
questions.solution: Lead (Pb) is a comparatively poor conductor of heat and electricity; silver, copper and aluminium are among the best conductors.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The natural sources of oxalic acid, lactic acid and methanoic acid respectively are :
questions.solution: Oxalic acid is found in tomato, lactic acid in curd (sour milk) and methanoic acid in ant sting (and nettle sting). Only option A has all three right.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: When an element 'X' reacts with water, it starts floating. Identify the element 'X' :
questions.solution: Calcium reacts less violently with water; the bubbles of hydrogen formed stick to its surface and make it float.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Carbon shares its valence electrons with other atoms of carbon or with atoms of other elements.
Reason (R): The shared electrons belong to the outermost shells of both the atoms and lead to both atoms attaining the noble gas configuration.
options: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Carbon forms covalent bonds by sharing electrons, and it does so because sharing lets both atoms reach a noble gas configuration. So R correctly explains A.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm, is forming a real image. If the size of image is same as the size of object, then position of object and position of image will be, respectively :
questions.solution: A same-size real image forms when the object is at 2F: u = −2f = −30 cm and v = +30 cm.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text: When you look at an object very close to your eyes, the :
options: Ciliary muscles of your eye contract and the eye lens becomes thick.
Ciliary muscles of your eye get relaxed and the eye lens becomes thick.
Ciliary muscles of your eye contract and the eye lens becomes thin.
Ciliary muscles of your eye get relaxed and the eye lens becomes thin.
questions.solution: For near objects the ciliary muscles contract, the lens becomes thicker and its focal length decreases (accommodation).

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text:
Assertion (A): When rays of white light pass through a prism, on emerging they give spectrum of seven colours.
Reason (R): It is due to the scattering of light that red light bends minimum and violet light bends the maximum.
options: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: A prism splits white light into seven colours, so A is true. This is due to dispersion (different colours refract by different amounts), not scattering, so R is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is the function of diaphragm in human respiratory system ? Where is it present in human body ?
questions.solution: When we breathe in, the diaphragm (a muscular sheet) contracts and flattens, enlarging the chest cavity so air is drawn into the lungs; when it relaxes, air is pushed out. It lies below the lungs, separating the chest (thoracic) cavity from the abdominal cavity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: State two differences between the act of chewing food and salivation on sight of food.
questions.solution: Chewing is a voluntary action (we decide to do it), controlled by the cerebrum; it breaks food down mechanically with teeth and jaw muscles. Salivation on seeing food is involuntary (a reflex), controlled by the hindbrain (medulla); it is the secretion of saliva by the salivary glands.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: State two differences between pollination and fertilization.
questions.solution: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma; it happens on the surface of the flower and comes first. Fertilisation is the fusion of the male germ cell with the female germ cell (egg) inside the ovule; it happens after pollination and forms the zygote.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
A pyramid shows four trophic levels in an ecosystem : (i) Producers, (ii) Primary consumers, (iii) Secondary consumers, (iv) Tertiary consumers.
(a) From the organisms listed below, identify which one is to be placed at which trophic level ? Deer, Grass, Lion, Snake, Rabbit
(b) Discuss the reason why primary consumers will have more energy as compared to secondary consumers ?
(c) Why is the base of the pyramid broad ?
questions.solution: (a) (i) Producers: grass; (ii) primary consumers: deer and rabbit; (iii) secondary consumers: snake; (iv) tertiary consumers: lion. (b) Only about 10% of the energy at one level passes to the next; the rest is used in life processes or lost as heat. So primary consumers have more energy than secondary consumers. (c) Producers capture the most energy and are the most numerous, and the energy and number decrease at each higher level, so the base is the widest.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Give differences between the following : (a) Nephron and neuron (b) Sensory nerve and motor nerve (c) Consumers and decomposers
questions.solution: (a) A nephron is the filtering unit of the kidney (removes wastes and forms urine); a neuron is the unit of the nervous system (carries nerve impulses). (b) A sensory nerve carries impulses from receptors (sense organs) to the brain or spinal cord; a motor nerve carries impulses from the brain or spinal cord to effectors (muscles and glands). (c) Consumers get their food by eating other organisms (herbivores, carnivores); decomposers, such as bacteria and fungi, break down dead remains and wastes into simple substances, returning nutrients to the soil.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Given below are certain situations. Analyse each and describe its possible impact :
(i) A population of bacteria living in temperate waters whose temperature increased by global warming.
(ii) The sperm encounters the egg when it reaches the oviduct in human females.
(iii) Self pollination does not occur in a flower that contains only pistil.
(iv) Egg does not get fertilised in a human female.
(v) When the seed is placed under appropriate condition of water and air in the soil ?
questions.solution: (i) Most of the bacteria may die; only those with variations that let them tolerate heat survive and multiply, so variation helps the species survive. (ii) Fertilisation takes place and a zygote forms, which later implants in the uterus. (iii) The flower is unisexual (female), so it needs cross-pollination by pollen from another flower. (iv) The thickened lining of the uterus breaks down and is shed as blood and mucus (menstruation). (v) The seed germinates: the embryo grows into a seedling, using the stored food.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Given below are certain situations. Analyse and describe what would happen when :
(i) Spores are liberated from blob-like structures of the bread mould?
(ii) Leaves of bryophyllum fall on wet soil ?
(iii) A pollen from different species land on the stigma of totally unrelated species ?
(iv) Copper-T is placed in the uterus of a human female ?
(v) Spirogyra breaks into smaller fragments upon maturation ?
questions.solution: (i) The spores, released from the sporangia of Rhizopus, land on moist food and grow into new mould. (ii) Buds in the notches of the leaf margin grow into new plants (vegetative propagation). (iii) Fertilisation does not take place, because the pollen of an unrelated species cannot grow a pollen tube on that stigma. (iv) It prevents pregnancy by stopping implantation (it may cause irritation of the uterus). (v) Each fragment grows into a new Spirogyra filament (fragmentation).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) What are amphoteric oxides ?
(b) Categorise the following based on their nature : ZnO, Na₂O, CO₂
questions.solution: (a) Oxides that react with both acids and bases to form salt and water (for example Al₂O₃ and ZnO). (b) ZnO is amphoteric, Na₂O is basic and CO₂ is acidic.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Name the substance oxidised and reduced in the following reaction : ZnO + C → Zn + CO
(b) Balance the following chemical reaction : Pb(NO₃)₂ + KI → PbI₂ + KNO₃
(c) Give one example each of electrolytic decomposition and decomposition by sunlight.
questions.solution: (a) Carbon is oxidised (to CO) and zinc oxide is reduced (to Zn). (b) Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂ + 2KNO₃. (c) Electrolytic: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂ (electrolysis of water). By sunlight: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂ (or 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br₂).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Explain chlor-alkali process with chemical equation. Name the products formed at anode and cathode.
questions.solution: When electricity is passed through brine (concentrated aqueous NaCl), it decomposes to give sodium hydroxide, chlorine and hydrogen: 2NaCl(aq) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl₂(g) + H₂(g). It is called chlor-alkali because of the products: chlorine and an alkali. Chlorine gas forms at the anode and hydrogen gas at the cathode; sodium hydroxide solution forms near the cathode.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Write the preparation of following compounds with balanced chemical equation : (i) Baking soda (ii) Bleaching powder (iii) Plaster of Paris
questions.solution: (i) Baking soda: NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃. (ii) Bleaching powder: chlorine is passed over dry slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O. (iii) Plaster of Paris: gypsum is heated at 373 K, CaSO₄·2H₂O → CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Give reasons for the following : (I) Covalent compounds are poor conductor of electricity. (II) Soap does not form lather in hard water. (III) Carbon shows catenation but silicon does not.
(ii) Write chemical equations for the following : (I) Oxidation of ethanol by acidified K₂Cr₂O₇. (II) Hydrogenation of ethene.
questions.solution: (i) (I) Covalent compounds are made of molecules, not ions, so there are no charged particles to carry current. (II) Hard water contains calcium and magnesium salts, which react with soap to form an insoluble scum instead of lather. (III) Carbon–carbon bonds are very strong and stable because carbon atoms are small, so carbon can form long chains; Si–Si bonds are weaker, so silicon forms only short chains that are reactive. (ii) (I) CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOH (acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, heat). (II) CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃–CH₃ (nickel catalyst).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mohan heated ethanol with a compound 'X' in the presence of a few drops of conc. H₂SO₄ and observed a sweet smelling compound 'Y' is formed. When 'Y' is treated with sodium hydroxide it gives back ethanol and a compound 'Z'.
(i) Identify 'X', 'Y' and 'Z'.
(ii) Write the role of conc. H₂SO₄ in the reaction.
(iii) Write the chemical equations involved and name the reactions.
questions.solution: (i) X = ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH), Y = ethyl ethanoate (an ester, CH₃COOC₂H₅), Z = sodium ethanoate (CH₃COONa). (ii) Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as a catalyst (and dehydrating agent). (iii) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O (esterification). CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → C₂H₅OH + CH₃COONa (saponification).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The resistance of a wire of 0.01 cm radius and 1.0 cm length is 7 Ω. Calculate its resistivity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An electric heater is rated 220 V; 11 A. Calculate the power consumed if the heater is operated at 200 V.
questions.solution: Resistance R = V/I = 220 ÷ 11 = 20 Ω. At 200 V, P = V²/R = 200² ÷ 20 = 2000 W.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text: A person is unable to read a book placed closer than 1 meter from his eyes. Identify the defect of vision in his eyes. Draw the ray diagrams to show the defect of vision and its correction.
questions.solution: The defect is hypermetropia (long-sightedness): the near point has moved beyond 25 cm (here to 1 m). Defect diagram: rays from a nearby object focus behind the retina. Correction diagram: a convex (converging) lens of suitable power in front of the eye makes the rays from the object at 25 cm appear to come from the near point, so they focus on the retina.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Describe an activity to show that a current carrying conductor, placed in an external magnetic field experiences a force.
(b) Imagine that you are sitting in a chamber with your back to one wall. An electron beam, moving horizontally towards the front wall from the back wall, is deflected by a strong magnetic field to your right side. Find the direction of the magnetic field.
questions.solution: (a) Hang a small aluminium rod horizontally between the poles of a horseshoe magnet and connect it to a battery through a key. When current flows, the rod moves (is displaced). Reversing the current or the magnet's poles reverses the direction of movement, showing that the conductor experiences a force. (b) Electrons move towards the front wall, so the current is towards the back wall. The force is to the right. By Fleming's left-hand rule (middle finger along the current, thumb along the force), the magnetic field points vertically downward.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Due to change in length and area of cross-section of a conductor, resistance of conductor changes while resistivity does not change. Why ?
(ii) Conductors of electric toasters and electric iron are made of an alloy rather than a pure metal. Why ?
(iii) Define the S.I. unit of electric current.
questions.solution: (i) Resistance R = ρl/A depends on the length and area, but resistivity ρ is a property of the material itself (and temperature), so it stays the same. (ii) Alloys have higher resistivity than pure metals and do not oxidise (burn) readily at high temperatures. (iii) The SI unit of current is the ampere: 1 A flows when 1 coulomb of charge passes through a cross-section of a conductor in 1 second.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) How many bulbs of resistance 8 Ω each should be connected in parallel combination to draw a current of 2 A from a battery of 4 V ?
(ii) Name the device used for measuring electric current. How is it connected in a circuit ?
(iii) State Joule's law of heating.
questions.solution: (i) Required resistance R = V/I = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 Ω. n bulbs of 8 Ω in parallel give 8/n = 2, so n = 4 bulbs. (ii) An ammeter, connected in series in the circuit. (iii) The heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of the current, to the resistance and to the time for which the current flows: H = I²Rt.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mendel took garden pea plants with different characteristics, such as height to study the inheritance pattern of factors (genes). He crossed tall pea plant with short pea plant and obtained all the tall plants in the F₁ generation.

Why only tall pea plants were observed in F₁ progeny ?
questions.solution: Tallness is the dominant trait. Every F₁ plant got one 'tall' and one 'short' factor (Tt), and the dominant tall factor is the one expressed.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mendel took garden pea plants with different characteristics, such as height to study the inheritance pattern of factors (genes). He crossed tall pea plant with short pea plant and obtained all the tall plants in the F₁ generation.

By which method did Mendel obtain F₂ progeny ?
questions.solution: By self-pollination of the F₁ plants.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mendel took garden pea plants with different characteristics, such as height to study the inheritance pattern of factors (genes). He crossed tall pea plant with short pea plant and obtained all the tall plants in the F₁ generation.

Write one difference between dominant and recessive trait.
questions.solution: A dominant trait is expressed even when only one copy of its factor is present (Tt is tall); a recessive trait is expressed only when both copies are recessive (tt).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mendel took garden pea plants with different characteristics, such as height to study the inheritance pattern of factors (genes). He crossed tall pea plant with short pea plant and obtained all the tall plants in the F₁ generation.

Write two observations made by Mendel about F₁ progeny.
questions.solution: All the F₁ plants were tall, and there were no plants of medium (in-between) height: only one of the parental traits was seen.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Most of metals occur in combined state in form of ores. Carbonate ores are converted into oxides by calcination and sulphide ores by roasting. Oxides are reduced with suitable reducing agent like carbon to get free metal. Highly reactive metals like Al, Mg are also used as reducing agents to obtain metal from their oxides. Most reactive metals are obtained by electrolytic reduction of their molten ores. Alloying is a very good method of improving the properties of a metal. We can get desired properties by this method. The electrical conductivity and melting point of an alloy is less than that of pure metals.

Why carbonate or sulphide ores are converted to oxides before extraction of metal from it ?
questions.solution: It is easier to obtain a metal from its oxide (by reduction) than from its carbonate or sulphide.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Most of metals occur in combined state in form of ores. Oxides are reduced with suitable reducing agent like carbon to get free metal. Highly reactive metals like Al, Mg are also used as reducing agents to obtain metal from their oxides.

Write a reaction in which Aluminium is used as a reducing agent to obtain metal from its oxide.
questions.solution: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → 2Fe + Al₂O₃ + heat (thermite reaction). (Also 3MnO₂ + 4Al → 3Mn + 2Al₂O₃.)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Most of metals occur in combined state in form of ores. Carbonate ores are converted into oxides by calcination and sulphide ores by roasting. Oxides are reduced with suitable reducing agent like carbon to get free metal.

How is copper obtained from its ore (Cu₂S) ? Give equations of the reactions.
questions.solution: Copper glance is heated in air (roasting), partly converting it to copper(I) oxide: 2Cu₂S + 3O₂ → 2Cu₂O + 2SO₂. The oxide then reacts with the remaining sulphide to give copper metal: 2Cu₂O + Cu₂S → 6Cu + SO₂.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Most reactive metals are obtained by electrolytic reduction of their molten ores. Alloying is a very good method of improving the properties of a metal. The electrical conductivity and melting point of an alloy is less than that of pure metals.

(I) Why highly reactive metals cannot be obtained from their oxides by using carbon as a reducing agent ?
(II) Why solder, an alloy of lead and tin, is used for welding electrical wires together ?
questions.solution: (I) Highly reactive metals have a greater affinity for oxygen than carbon has, so carbon cannot reduce their oxides. (II) Solder has a low melting point, so it melts easily and joins the wires without damaging them.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Lenses can form different types of images depending upon their focal length and position of object. A convex lens can create real, inverted or virtual, erect images, while a concave lens forms only virtual and diminished images. The focal length determines the power of lens. Convex lenses have positive focal length while concave lenses have negative focal length by convention. When lenses are placed together, their combined power is determined by the sum of their individual powers.

A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is used to form an image. If an object is placed at 40 cm from the lens, what will be the position and nature of image ?
questions.solution: The object is at 2F (40 cm = 2 × 20 cm), so the image is at 2F on the other side, 40 cm from the lens; it is real, inverted and the same size as the object.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Lenses can form different types of images depending upon their focal length and position of object. A convex lens can create real, inverted or virtual, erect images, while a concave lens forms only virtual and diminished images.

Illustrate the formation of image with the help of ray diagram, when the object is placed between the optical centre and principal focus of concave lens.
questions.solution: A ray parallel to the axis diverges after refraction as if coming from the focus F₁; a ray through the optical centre goes straight on. The refracted rays appear to meet on the same side as the object, between O and F₁. The image is virtual, erect and diminished.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The focal length determines the power of lens. Convex lenses have positive focal length while concave lenses have negative focal length by convention. When lenses are placed together, their combined power is determined by the sum of their individual powers.

A lens combination consists of a convex lens of focal length 30 cm and a concave lens of focal length 15 cm placed together. Find the equivalent focal length and power of this lens combination.
questions.solution: P₁ = 1/0.30 m = +3.33 D and P₂ = 1/(−0.15 m) = −6.67 D. Combined power P = −3.33 D. Equivalent focal length = 1/P = −0.30 m = −30 cm (a diverging combination).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The focal length determines the power of lens. Convex lenses have positive focal length while concave lenses have negative focal length by convention. When lenses are placed together, their combined power is determined by the sum of their individual powers.

Two lenses are placed in contact. One is a concave lens with focal length 2 m and the other is a convex lens with focal length 1.5 m. What type of lens will the combination behave as (convex or concave) ? Give reason.
questions.solution: P = 1/(−2) + 1/1.5 = −0.5 + 0.67 = +0.17 D. The combined power is positive, so the combination behaves as a convex (converging) lens.
